title: Pass the handler, don't call it

slides.say: One tiny pair of parentheses can make your click handler fire without any click.
Without parentheses, you pass the function, and React calls it on click. With parentheses, it runs immediately, during rendering.
Inline code has the same trap. Wrap it in an arrow function, so you create a function to be called later.

slides.text: onClick wants a function, not the result of calling one.
slides.say: Takeaway: onClick wants a function, not the result of calling one.
